name: Adrian Sherwood
hook: A London teenager who took the Jamaican dub studio's tricks and built a British label out of them.
blurb: Sherwood founded On-U Sound in London in 1979, a label built around the dub techniques King Tubby and Lee Perry had pioneered in Kingston: heavy echo, vocals that drop out, the studio used as an instrument. He applied them to a changing cast of Jamaican session players and British post-punk musicians working together in London studios. Bands like African Head Charge and Tackhead used his production to mix dub with punk, funk and industrial noise. He is the clearest case of dub's techniques living on far from the place and the business that made them, carried into British industrial and dance music through the 1980s and beyond.
